break.lookFarHint: Out of the window or at a far wall, more than 6 metres (20 feet) away. The muscle that holds close focus gets to rest.
break.standUpHint: A couple of exercises for your back and legs, then walk around.
break.walkHint: To the window, for water, up the stairs. Drink some water too.
break.longHint: Step away from the computer: walk, have lunch, go outside. The screen can wait.
break.neckTitle: Two minutes for neck and shoulders
break.neckHint: A short strength routine once a day. Move slowly.
break.breathHint: Follow the circle: breathe in for 4, out for 6.
break.noPain: No pain. If it hurts, stop.
tips: Keep the screen at arm's length, 50–70 cm (20–28 inches).
Keep the top of the screen at eye level or a little below. Looking slightly down keeps the eye less open, so it dries out less.
Air conditioners and fans should not blow into your face. A humidifier helps in winter.
Match screen brightness to the room light. A bright screen in a dark room is more tiring.
Make the font bigger if you catch yourself squinting.
Artificial tear drops should be chosen by a doctor, not by yourself.
Change position often. The best posture is the next one.
Keep the mouse next to the keyboard so you don't reach for it.
At lunch, get at least 10 minutes of daylight outside.

eyes.text: At a screen we blink 2–3 times less often, and half the blinks are incomplete, so the eyes dry out. The muscle that holds close focus doesn't rest for hours. Reminders to look into the distance reduce burning and eye fatigue.
eyes.doctor: if your eyes hurt, are red, you see double or your vision gets worse.

neck.text: Sitting for long with the head slightly forward keeps the neck and shoulder muscles a little tense all the time. Short strength exercises help most: even 2 minutes a day reduces pain.
neck.doctor: if pain or numbness goes into the arm, the arm gets weak, or pain lasts more than 6 weeks.

back.text: It's not a "wrong" posture that harms the back, it's not moving. The best posture is the next one. Short walks every 20–30 minutes also lower blood sugar after meals.
back.doctor: if you feel numb in the groin, your legs get weak, the pain is severe at night or lasts 4–6 weeks.

hands.text: Forearm muscles work without rest, the wrist is often bent. Breaks every 20 minutes reduce discomfort in the arms. A link between computer use and carpal tunnel syndrome is not proven, so we don't promise to prevent it.
hands.doctor: if your thumb, index and middle fingers go numb, especially at night, or you drop things.

legs.text: Calf muscles work as a pump that moves blood out of the legs. Sitting switches the pump off, and by evening the legs swell. Standing up and walking at least once an hour helps.
legs.doctor: urgently, if one leg is swollen, painful and red, or you get short of breath with chest pain.

breath.text: Slow breathing, about 6 breaths a minute with a long exhale, lowers tension. The effect is small but noticeable within minutes.
breath.doctor: if anxiety has been getting in the way of life for weeks: breathing is not a replacement for professional help.

water.text: Even mild lack of water worsens attention and mood, and can cause a headache. We don't push a daily amount: go by thirst. Tea and coffee count too.
water.doctor: if a doctor limited your fluids, follow their advice and turn this reminder off.

workplace.text: A well set-up workstation removes some discomfort but by itself does little. Breaks and movement do more.
workplace.doctor: if pain continues after setting up the workstation and taking breaks.

share.footer: Unslouch: a free app for health at the computer · unslouch.health-diet.ru

about.text: The app reminds you of what doctors recommend to people who spend all day at a computer: blink more often, every 20 minutes look into the distance for 20 seconds, stand up and move, stretch your neck, shoulders and hands, drink water.
about.disclaimer: The app does not treat anything and does not replace a doctor. Do the exercises without pain. If something hurts, goes numb, or your vision gets worse, see a doctor.
about.privacyShort: We don't collect any data: everything stays on your computer.
about.asIs: The app is provided "as is", without warranties, and you use it at your own risk. See the terms of use.
